subject: PulseHealth — performance qualification & streaming cadence next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@pulsehealth.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@pulsehealth.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: PulseHealth — performance qualification & streaming cadence next steps

Hi Emma / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have shared expectations before we run any benchmarks. I captured what I heard on your targets and constraints below. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of requirements (from call)
- Primary objective: reduce perceived latency for clinician-facing chat widget and ensure stable streaming for long form summaries.
- Target time-to-first-token (TTFT): <= 120ms for short prompts (single-turn triage), up to 200ms acceptable for longer context responses.
- Streaming cadence: small, frequent chunks to make UI feel instantaneous — target ~120–250ms between chunks for desktop web session; mobile can tolerate slightly higher cadence (~200–350ms).
- Throughput & concurrency: 40 sustained concurrent live sessions during peak, burst to ~120 concurrent for flash loads; average sustained throughput ~600 requests/min.
- Reliability: prefer graceful degradation with a cheaper model fallback vs. hard error.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood to run a two-day microbenchmark against a representative prompt set (we'll use the sample prompts you shared + the two critical templates). We'll measure TTFT, chunk cadence, and end-to-end time across our hosted and dedicated configs.
2) PulseHealth to confirm which client protocol you prefer for the clinician UI: SSE (EventSource) or WebSocket. From our experience SSE is simpler for browser-based streaming but WebSocket works better if you need bidirectional low-latency interactivity or binary payloads.
3) Align on acceptance criteria: TTFT <= 120ms for triage flows, 90% of streaming chunks delivered at cadence < 300ms, and no more than 1% error rate over sustained load.
4) Schedule a 30-minute results review call after the benchmark completes (suggest Mon Nov 23 afternoon PT).

Attachments: I attached a one-page SLO checklist and a JSON with the cadence/measurements we'll capture.

Action items
- Emma/Rajiv: confirm protocol preference (SSE vs WebSocket) and give final sample prompt set by EOD Monday.
- Aditya: can you prepare the benchmark config (model variant, token limits, seq len, concurrency profile) once we have final prompts?

Thanks — appreciate the quick sync.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Emma Walsh <emma@pulsehealth.ai>

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseHealth — performance qualification & streaming cadence next steps

Thanks Soojin — this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Protocol: prefer SSE for the clinician web UI (we're using a React SPA with EventSource already wired). We may test WebSocket later for our mobile app, but primary is SSE.
- Prompts: will confirm final set Monday morning; initial set includes triage prompt (<= 120 tokens), note-summarization (250–400 tokens), and a combined-long-context summary used in discharge notes (~800 tokens).
- TTFT expectation: the 120ms target for triage is targeted at the triage prompt only. For note-summarization and discharge summaries we accept up to 220ms TTFT, provided streaming chunk cadence is smooth.
- Concurrency: peak numbers are estimates — 40 concurrent clinicians in typical peak zone; the 120 burst is when several units hit the system during shift change.

We approve the two-day microbenchmark. Please include a simulated browser client (SSE) and a WebSocket run so we can compare.

Thanks,
Emma
Director of Product — PulseHealth
emma@pulsehealth.ai

--Forwarded note: will attach final prompt set Monday.
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@pulsehealth.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@pulsehealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseHealth — performance qualification & streaming cadence next steps

Great — thanks for confirming SSE as primary. Looping Aditya and Sean from infra/solutions so they can start configuration and capacity planning.

Aditya / Sean — two quick clarifications for the benchmark config:
1) Model variant: Emma mentioned higher quality is needed for summaries; propose we run the benchmark against model-xl-32q (quantized) and model-xl-8bit (lower memory) so we can show tradeoffs in TTFT and token cost.
2) Sequence lengths: run three buckets — short (<= 128 tokens), mid (250–450 tokens), long (up to 1024 tokens) to reflect the triage, summaries, and discharge flows.
3) Chunk cadence sampling: capture inter-chunk latency distribution and make a small-sample trace (100 representative requests per bucket). We'll compute p50/p90/p99 for TTFT and inter-chunk intervals.
4) Concurrency profile: baseline 40 concurrent sustained with 10 RPS per concurrent session for the burst window to simulate 120 concurrent. Use our prefix caching where applicable.

Emma — we'll send the exact test harness (load script + client simulator) by Monday morning. If you can send the final prompts and a short recording of the real UI network behavior that helps us calibrate the client-side chunking.

I'll schedule the results review for Mon Nov 23 3:00pm PT; if that doesn't work we'll move to Tue.

Soojin
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Walsh <emma@pulsehealth.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@pulsehealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseHealth — performance qualification & streaming cadence next steps

Quick plan from infra side — we'll kick off runs tonight (sandbox) and run two full waves tomorrow (hosted endpoint + dedicated reserve) as agreed. Deliverables and checkpoints:

A) Benchmark config (delivered Mon 06:30 PT) — includes: model variants, sequence buckets, seed prompts, concurrency schedule, and the client simulator (SSE + WebSocket toggles).
B) Raw measurements (delivered Tue morning) — CSVs with per-request TTFT, per-chunk timestamps, and per-run p50/p90/p99.
C) Short analysis (delivered Tue by 11:00 PT) — one-pager with recommendations: best-fit model variant for your SLOs, expected costs (tokens + infra) and suggested fallback policy (model fallback + cached prefixes).

Notes on what we'll look for specifically:
- TTFT: measuring both server-side first-token emission and end-to-end browser-rendered first chunk (we instrument client simulator to capture EventSource onmessage receipt).
- Chunk cadence: we'll compute inter-chunk interval histogram and flag any large gaps > 800ms.
- Fallback behavior: demonstration of automatic fallback to model-xl-8bit when p99 latency of primary variant exceeds 500ms.

Emma / Rajiv — we'll need the final prompt set and any UI-level instrumentation you can provide (network logs or HAR export). If we don't get prompts by EOD Monday we'll use the sample prompts you shared on the call.

Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
